A bill for an act relating to housing; providing rights to tenants when a landlord has received funding to assist with renovations of a residential rental unit; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 504B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+[504B.267] HOMEOWNER RENOVATION ASSISTANCE; NONRENEWAL PROHIBITED. +]

[+(a) A landlord who receives federal, state, or local government assistance, including assistance that is awarded through a housing redevelopment authority or nonprofit, to renovate a rental unit to accommodate the health, safety, or disability of a tenant, must allow the tenant to continue to reside in the unit. A nonrenewal of lease provided to a tenant in violation of this section is void and a landlord is liable for any costs incurred by a tenant when a landlord has violated this section, including attorney fees and costs. +]

[+(b) Nothing in this section prevents a landlord from pursuing an eviction action that is otherwise allowed under this chapter. +]

[+(c) A rental increase that the court finds to be unreasonable or disproportionate may be considered a constructive nonrenewal and is a violation of this section. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to housing; providing rights to tenants when a landlord has received funding to assist with renovations of a residential rental unit; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 504B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[504B.267] HOMEOWNER RENOVATION ASSISTANCE; NONRENEWAL PROHIBITED.

(a) A landlord who receives federal, state, or local government assistance, including assistance that is awarded through a housing redevelopment authority or nonprofit, to renovate a rental unit to accommodate the health, safety, or disability of a tenant, must allow the tenant to continue to reside in the unit. A nonrenewal of lease provided to a tenant in violation of this section is void and a landlord is liable for any costs incurred by a tenant when a landlord has violated this section, including attorney fees and costs.

(b) Nothing in this section prevents a landlord from pursuing an eviction action that is otherwise allowed under this chapter.

(c) A rental increase that the court finds to be unreasonable or disproportionate may be considered a constructive nonrenewal and is a violation of this section.
additions: (a) A landlord who receives federal, state, or local government assistance, including assistance that is awarded through a housing redevelopment authority or nonprofit, to renovate a rental unit to accommodate the health, safety, or disability of a tenant, must allow the tenant to continue to reside in the unit. A nonrenewal of lease provided to a tenant in violation of this section is void and a landlord is liable for any costs incurred by a tenant when a landlord has violated this section, including attorney fees and costs.
(b) Nothing in this section prevents a landlord from pursuing an eviction action that is otherwise allowed under this chapter.
(c) A rental increase that the court finds to be unreasonable or disproportionate may be considered a constructive nonrenewal and is a violation of this section.
